title: The African diaspora
summary: Plantation systems built on enslaved labour spread across the Atlantic, reaching Brazil in the late 16th century, after European diseases had killed many Indigenous people. UNESCO estimates that 900,000 Africans arrived in South America through Valongo Wharf in Rio de Janeiro alone, built from 1811 as their landing place.

uncertainty.note: Covers the early modern and modern era of the transatlantic African diaspora, from 16th-century plantation expansion to the late 19th-century abolition of slavery in the Americas.

importance.justification: The forced dispersal of millions of Africans across the Atlantic created worldwide diasporic communities that transformed global demographics, culture, and economies.

audience_note: Concerns the transatlantic slave trade and the forced dispersal of enslaved Africans; describes historical migration, labor, and cultural impact without graphic detail.

related.because: The transatlantic slave trade served as the forced commercial mechanism that physically transported millions of Africans to the Americas.
